title: Resumable windowed streaming and language-agnostic client interop spec
creator: Ava Martinez
description: PRD for a unified SDK contract enabling resumable, windowed streaming across Python, TypeScript, and Go clients. The goal is to allow product teams to integrate long-running streaming outputs (for example, multi-minute generation with intermittent connectivity) with deterministic resume semantics, language idiomatic surfaces, and clear downgrade behavior when consumers are running older SDK versions or older server runtimes. This ticket captures requirements, acceptance criteria, API sketches, test plan, and rollout guidance.
background: Customers building chat assistants and live transcription pipelines have reported production incidents when long-lived streams are interrupted by transient network failures or client restarts. Current SDKs either rely on best-effort reconnection or require full restart of generation, which causes duplicated tokens or loss of context. We need a consistent cross-language contract that supports: windowed checkpoints (KV cache offsets), idempotent resume tokens, server-side compatible fallbacks, and clear degradation policy for older clients/servers.
goals: Define a minimal set of stream primitives (open, window, checkpoint, resume, close) that map to idiomatic Python/TS/Go APIs
Ensure resume tokens are stable across minor server releases and include cryptographic HMAC to prevent replay/falsification
Specify downgrade behavior: how older SDK versions should fall back to chunked or non-resumable streams with clear error semantics
Create acceptance tests and backward-compatibility matrix to validate cross-version interactions
Provide rollout plan with feature flags and telemetry to monitor resume success rates
non_goals: This PRD does not mandate a single on-disk persistence format for resume tokens (clients may choose memory, filesystem, or secure key stores)
Does not change model-level decoding or require model checkpoints beyond KV-cache offsets
Does not define UI controls for end-user reconnection (product teams will implement UX)
requirements: Functional: Server must issue a resumable token after the first successful window acknowledgement. Token is opaque to clients but contains version metadata and an HMAC with per-customer key version id.

Functional: Clients must be able to request resume(token) and receive both a: validation result and b: a delta stream starting from the resumed offset. If server cannot resume, it must return a clear recoverable error code (409) with suggested fallbacks.
Functional: SDKs must expose a structured envelope for each chunk: {seq, window_start_offset, window_end_offset, data, checkpoint_hint}. All SDKs should surface seq and checkpoint_hint consistently.

Retry semantics: Clients must use exponential backoff with jitter for resume attempts (base=200ms, max=6s, attempts=5) and classify resume errors as transient vs permanent based on server-provided codes.

Pagination & streaming interplay: For list-like streaming endpoints (e.g., paged logs over a time window), design must allow combining cursor pagination with resume tokens so that a resumed stream correctly continues from the paged cursor position.
Compatibility: Server must maintain resume token decoding for n major versions (n=2 by default) and include token version in the opaque blob to allow safe parsing and fallback.
Observability: Clients must emit telemetry events: stream_open, window_ack, resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_failure, fallback_to_nonresumable.
Security: Resume tokens must be bound to customer and model id and should expire after a configurable TTL (default 24 hours).
api_sketch_python:
# Python idiomatic sketch
from redwood import StreamingClient

client = StreamingClient(api_key=... )

# start a windowed stream
stream = client.start_stream(model="rwd-large-2", window_size=256)

for chunk in stream:
    if chunk.checkpoint_hint:
        # persist resume token atomically with local cursor
        persist(chunk.checkpoint_hint.token)

# resume later
resume_token = load_saved_token()
stream = client.resume_stream(resume_token)
compatibility_matrix: Server v1.x + Client v1.x: full resumable streams supported
Server v1.x + Client v0.y (older): client should detect missing resume support via capability header and automatically fall back to opaque non-resumable streaming with a deprecation warning
Server v2.x + Client v1.x: tokens from v2 are recognized; server maintains v1 compatibility for 2 minor releases
Cross-language: Token format is opaque; implementations must not attempt to deserialize tokens except to surface version string for diagnostics
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests for Python/TS/Go clients that cover: initial stream open, window acknowledgements, persisting checkpoint tokens, successful resume, resume rejected with specific error code, and fallback path
E2E test where network is interrupted at varying offsets (randomized) and client resumes successfully within 5 attempts 95% of the time in CI synthetic workload
Backward-compatibility tests: server v1.9 can resume tokens minted by server v1.8; server v2.0 rejects v0 tokens with defined error code and recommended client fallback path
Telemetry events for resume_success/resume_failure appear in staging dashboards and have instrumentation tests asserting event fields are present
Security review signoff for token HMAC strategy and TTL handling
scope_notes: Scope includes SDK surface changes, server-side token issuance and validation, and staging test harness. Out of scope: client OS-level persistence standards, UI/UX for reconnection buttons, and durable storage recommendations beyond examples.
tech_notes: Server will include a capability header 'X-RW-Streaming-Resume: v1' on stream start. Tokens will be signed using a rotating HMAC key tied to customer id. Clients will not be required to verify signature locally; server will validate on resume. We will reuse existing telemetry schema for event names to minimize instrument churn.
testing_plan: Add unit tests in each SDK repo for token persistence and resume logic
Create chaos test harness in staging that terminates TCP at random intervals for simulated long streams
Add post-deploy smoke test that runs resume scenarios against canary servers
Include compatibility matrix checks in nightly integration pipeline
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated on server side per account; 2) Release SDK clients with opt-in resume=true default in minor releases; 3) Enable flag for low-volume customers in staging; 4) Ramp to broader traffic and monitor resume_success metric and error codes; 5) Gradual enforcement of token TTL and key rotation with migration window
monitoring_and_telemetry: Logs: structured resume failures with error_code, customer_id, model_id, token_version
Dashboards: per-customer success rate, 95th percentile resume latency, retry distribution
docs_and_client_migrations: Write migration guide for SDK consumers: how to persist tokens safely, recommended storage locations per platform, and examples for Python/TS/Go. Provide a compatibility table and a migration checklist for product engineers.
